data.paper_title: Illiquidity and stock returns: cross-section and time-series effects
data.selected_experiment: Table 2, Fama-MacBeth monthly cross-sectional regressions of NYSE stock returns on mean-adjusted ILLIQ (annual average of daily |return|/dollar volume) and other characteristics, 1964-1997

economic_rationale.value: Expected stock return increases in illiquidity, so stocks with higher ILLIQ (larger price impact per dollar of volume) earn a higher return as compensation for illiquidity.

universe_and_filters.value: NYSE-traded common stocks (CRSP), 1963-1997; stock needs a return in the month, more than 200 days of return and volume data in the prior year, listed at end of prior year, price above $5 at end of prior year, market cap available at end of prior year; stocks with ILLIQ in the top or bottom 1% tail are excluded

value: monthly stock returns (dependent variable, adjusted for delistings)
end-of-year market capitalization (SIZE control and listing filter)
number of days with return and volume data (filter)

signal_formula_words.value: ILLIQ for stock i in year y is the average over the year of the daily ratio of absolute return to dollar trading volume; it is divided by its cross-sectional mean in that year (ILLIQMA) before entering the regression

evidence.quote: Stock illiquidity is deﬁned here as the average ratio of the daily absolute

signal_formula_symbols.value: ILLIQ_iy = (1/D_iy) * sum over d=1..D_iy of |R_iyd| / VOLD_iyd; ILLIQMA_iy = ILLIQ_iy / AILLIQ_y

formation_window.value: 1 calendar year of daily returns and volume (year y-1)

holding_period.value: 1 month (each month of year y is regressed on characteristics from year y-1)

rebalance_frequency.value: monthly cross-sectional regressions; ILLIQ characteristic updated annually

evidence.quote: The monthly regressions of model (2) over the period

breakpoints.value: none; Fama-MacBeth cross-sectional regression on a continuous characteristic, no portfolio breakpoints

favored_group.value: stocks with high ILLIQ (most illiquid stocks; positive ILLIQMA coefficient)

disfavored_group.value: stocks with low ILLIQ (most liquid stocks)

headline_result.value: Mean ILLIQMA coefficient of 0.162 (t = 6.55) across 408 monthly regressions, 1964-1997, with only ILLIQMA, BETA, R100 and R100YR as regressors

evidence.quote: has a mean of 0.162 that is

unresolved_details: No portfolio sorts or breakpoints; the paper uses OLS regressions, so no long-short return is reported
Skip period between the end of the ILLIQ measurement year and the return month is not stated beyond the one-year lag
Return convention beyond the delisting-return adjustment (e.g. raw vs excess return) is not stated for the Table 2 dependent variable
Exact handling of days with zero volume is not stated
Treatment of share classes and security types beyond the market-cap data requirement is not stated
